proof sha256 b284f2d3. Re-derived by hand: label variance recursion V(t+1)=(1-r)^2(1-1/n)V(t)+p(1-p)/n so V<=p/(n alpha), alpha>=r and n alpha>=1; Gaussian part E W2^2(P_t,L_t)<=d h^2/r (mean kernel count <=1/r); annular inequality (1): normalization inequality sum|mu-(a/b)nu|<=sum|mu-nu|+(b-a) checked, unmatched product cost <=2d 4^k|a_k-b_k| from |x|^2<=d4^k, shell coefficient 2d+8d/3=14d/3<=8d; C002 dyadic lemma 2d on unit cube scales by 4^(k+1) to 8d 4^k, cells A_k cap dyadic still a tree; level sum (2): split j0=floor(log2(Np)/d) gives z/(z-1) x^(-2/d) + (8/3)4^(-(j0+1))<(8/3)x^(-2/d), Np<1 case 8/3; Markov P(A_k)<=2^(-q(k-1)) gives G exactly; affine scaling M^(2/q); triangle 2+2 gives 16d and 2dh^2, N^(-2/d)<=(nr)^(-2/d)<=n^(-2/d)/r. d>=5 and q>2d/(d-2) used exactly where stated. Rests on C002 (ancestor_coupling.md) which is itself unaudited: PASS is conditional on C002 v2 passing. Novelty: annular architecture is Fournier-Guillin 1312.2128 Lemmas 5-6, correctly cited, no novelty claimed.

proof sha256 701b553b (c002_v3.md byte-identical to ancestor_coupling.md). Re-derived: label construction gives the protocol marginal (t=1 synthetic branch draws from P_0=P); n Z_(t+1)|past ~ Bin(n, rp+(1-r)Z_t), total variance gives V(t+1)=aV(t)+p(1-p)/n with a=(1-1/n)(1-r)^2, closed form p(1-p)(1-a^t)/(n alpha) checked at t=1; alpha>=r and alpha>=1/n; D(t+1)=(1-r)(D_t+dh^2), D_1=0, so D_t+dh^2=dh^2(1-(1-r)^t)/r; dyadic lemma: bottom-up matching separates at level j at most half the level-j L1 discrepancy, distance^2 <= d 4^(-(j-1)), constant 2d on unit cube, L^2 on [0,L]^d; Cauchy-Schwarz over 2^(dj) cells; series split J=floor(log2 N/d): q^J<=N^(1/2-2/d) gives q/(q-1), tail (2/3)4^(-J)<=(8/3)N^(-2/d); 2A_d=4d(q/(q-1)+8/3) matches the statement. d>=5 needed only for q>1. Cosmetic: the last line of the file still says version 2. This PASS also discharges the C002 condition on the C004 v2 PASS.

proof sha256 f5bf3c63 (c005_v2.md byte-identical to protocol_transfer.md). Re-derived by hand: weighted protocol cond. mean rp+(1-r)Z_t, cond. var [r^2 p(1-p)+(1-r)^2 Z_t(1-Z_t)]/n (parents drawn from the weighted KDE, groups cond. independent); with E Z_t(1-Z_t)=p(1-p)-V_t this gives V_(t+1)=(1-1/n)(1-r)^2 V_t+s p(1-p)/n, V_1=s p(1-p)/n, fixed point s p(1-p)/(n alpha)<=p/(n alpha), recursion monotone so the bound holds for all t. Exact-count: Bin(m,p)+Bin(n-m,Z_t) gives a_m=(1-r)^2-(1-r)/n=(n-m)(n-m-1)/n^2>=0, a_B-a_m=r(1-r)/n, V_1=p(1-p)/n, so V_t<=p(1-p)/(n(1-a_m))<=p/(n alpha_B). Center displacement D_(t+1)=(1-r)(D_t+d h^2) in both (fresh centers 0, synthetic weight 1-r), so E W2^2(P_t,L_t)<=d h^2/r. These are exactly the three inputs C004 section 1 uses (E L_t(A)=P(A), Var<=P(A)/(n alpha), the W2 coupling) plus every label having marginal P (q moments = M), which holds for both protocols by induction; n alpha>=1 since alpha>=1/n. Scope statements (fresh data each round, no rounding for noninteger rn, n=1 weighted gives a_B=0) checked. No gaps.

proof sha256 88dc5eeb. Re-derived by hand: (B) W2^2(mu,Unif)=int(F-x)^2 for any mu on [0,1] via int Q^2=1-2 int xF and int uQ=1/2-(1/2)int F^2 (checked on delta_0: 1/3, delta_1/2: 1/12); U-parameter labels copied from parents give L_t=T#H_t with the KDE process unchanged; C002 cell recursion on [0,x] gives Var H_t([0,x])=x(1-x)(1-a^t)/(n alpha), so E W2^2(H_t,Unif)=(1-a^t)/(6n alpha)<=1/(6nr) (alpha>=r(2-r)>=r); Lipschitz pushforward W2^2(L_t,P)<=K^2 W2^2(H_t,Unif); squared triangle with C004 E W2^2(P_t,L_t)<=d h^2/r gives (A)=[K^2/(3n)+2d h^2]/r. d>=2 corollary (1/n<=n^(-2/d)) and d=1 corollary for h^2>=1/n (K^2/(3n)<=K^2 h^2/3) checked; weighted and exact-count variants covered by C005 (factor s<=1, a_m<=a). Fournier-Guillin arXiv:1312.2128 local text lines 134-139 read: the Lipschitz-image transfer remark is there as cited. Scope (Lipschitz T, fresh data, d=1 needs the bandwidth floor, 1/(6n) at t=1 h=0 rules out all-bandwidth n^-2) is correct. No gaps.

proof sha256 d1159cff (byte-identical to proofs/centered_variance.md). Re-derived by hand: divisor-n empirical covariance has expected trace (1-1/n)tr Cov, kernel adds d h^2, so v_(t+1)=a v_t+d h^2 and v_t=a^t v_0+n d h^2(1-a^t); mean martingale increments tr Cov(P_s)/n are orthogonal, E|m_t-m_0|^2=(1/n)sum_(s<t) v_s=v_0(1-a^t)+d h^2[t-n(1-a^t)] (geometric sums redone); adding v_t gives v_0+t d h^2. h=0: tail variance (1/n)sum_(s>=t) a^s v_0=a^t v_0, cross term zero since m_t is the mean of P_t, so E W2^2(P_t,delta_Minf)=2a^t v_0 (t=0 and n=1 checked: 2v_0). Joint scaling: a^(t_n)<=exp(-t_n/n); limits d lambda / infinity / exp(-tau)v_0+d lambda(1-exp(-tau)) correct; h_n=n^(-1/4) counterexample correct; iff for collapse correct. No gaps.

proof sha256 1a5c0aae. Corollary of C003 v2, re-derived: conclusion 1 from v_t formula with a_n^(t_n)<=exp(-t_n/n)->0 and n h_n^2->0; conclusion 2 remainder -v0 a_n^(t_n)-d n h_n^2(1-a_n^(t_n)) recomputed, bounded by v0 exp(-t_n/n)+d n h_n^2->0, valid even when t_n h_n^2 is unbounded; conclusion 3 by Jensen on each coupling then infimum then outer expectation. Example h_n=1/n, t_n=n^3 (t_n/n=n^2, n h_n^2=1/n, t_n h_n^2=n) correct. Claims are in expectation only, as stated. No gaps.

proof sha256 d8d60f5e. Target 1 read from brief: sup_t E W2^2 <= C(n^(-2/d)+h^2)/r. Re-derived by hand: two atoms, W2^2(P_n,P)=|B/n-1/2|; EZ^2=n/4, EZ^4=(3n^2-2n)/16; Holder E|Z|>=(EZ^2)^(3/2)/(EZ^4)^(1/2)>=sqrt(n)/(2 sqrt3); Gaussian coupling W2^2(P_n,Q_h)<=d h^2 and (a+b)^2<=2a^2+2b^2 give E W2^2(Q_h,P)>=1/(4 sqrt(3n))-d h^2; at h=1/n this is order n^(-1/2), which beats n^(-2/d) exactly for d<=3 (d=4 is not contradicted, matching the statement). Uniform [0,1]: variance part sum i(n+1-i)=n(n+1)(n+2)/6 gives 1/(6(n+1)); bias part with a_i-m_i=(n+1-2i)/(2n(n+1)) and sum (n+1-2i)^2=n(n^2-1)/3 gives 1/(6n(n+1)); total 1/(6n); so >=1/(12n)-h^2 against C*2/n^2 at h=1/n. r=1 makes every generation a fresh KDE, so sup_t is attained at t=1. Source checked: Fournier-Guillin arXiv:1312.2128v1 p.2 example (a) (papers/fournier_guillin.txt lines 97-102). Classical, no novelty; kind literature is right.

proof sha256 5b9e322e. Corollary of C002 v3 (dyadic lemma W2^2<=2d sum 4^-j sum|mu-nu| on [0,1]^d, scaled to side L gives 2dL^2; label cell second moment <=P(A)/(n alpha)) and C005 v2 (displacement <=d h^2/r), both PASS. Re-derived: alpha=1-(1-1/n)(1-r)^2 lies in [max(r,1/n),1], so 1<=N<=n and N>=nr. Cauchy-Schwarz over 2^(dj) cells gives E sum|L_t(B)-P(B)|<=2^(dj/2)/sqrt N, so level j costs 2dL^2 z_d^j N^(-1/2) with z_d=2^(d/2-2)<1 for d<=3 (0.354, 0.5, 0.707). Triangle squared plus N^(-1/2)<=n^(-1/2) r^(-1/2)<=n^(-1/2)/r<=h^2/r on h^2>=n^(-1/2) gives the stated constant. d=4: J=floor(log2 N/4); levels 1..J cost <=1/sqrt N each; tail 2 sum_{j>J}4^-j=(8/3)4^(-J-1)<=(8/3)N^(-1/2) since 4^(J+1)>=sqrt N iff J+1>=log2 N/4, true. log2 N<=log2 n; log2 n/4+8/3<=(8/3)(1+log2 n); absorbed by h^2>=n^(-1/2)(1+log2 n), giving (32d/3)L^2+2d with n^(-2/d)=n^(-1/2). n=1 boundary fine (N=1, J=0). Scope is honest: no small-bandwidth claim for d<4 (C001 excludes it) and none for d=4. NARROWED fits: a whole bandwidth interval of the named Target 1. Classical dyadic series; no novelty claim made.
